entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Cornelius Lentulus was a Roman politician and general who played a significant role in the late Republic.

As a member of the First Triumvirate, he collaborated with Julius Caesar and Pompey to shape Roman politics.

Lentulus's military campaigns were instrumental in maintaining Rome's dominance over Gaul, but his ultimate defeat at the Battle of Pharsalus led to his downfall.

Despite this, Lentulus's legacy endured through his influence on the development of Roman law and governance.

'Veni, Vidi, Vici,' Caesar famously said after his victory, but Lentulus himself never claimed such glory.
